title: Opening Edit Profile and pressing Save silently destroys the reducer and rewrites focal length / image scale by 25%
what_happened: The onboarding wizard let me set telescope FL 550 mm, aperture 100 mm and a 0.80x reducer; it correctly computed and stored effective FL 440.0 mm, f/4.4, image scale 1.76 arcsec/px. Equipment > Edit Profile has NO reducer/barlow field at all -- its Optical Train section only has Telescope/OTA, Focal Length and Aperture, and it displayed 'f/5.5' and 'Scale 1.41"/px at 3.76um'. I changed nothing and clicked 'Save Changes'. The DB went from focal_length=440.0, focal_ratio=4.4 to focal_length=550.0, focal_ratio=5.5. The reducer is now unrecoverable: no field anywhere in Edit Profile accepts it (AT-SPI tree of the whole dialog contains no 'Reducer' or 'Barlow' node), so the only place it can ever be entered is the one-time first-run wizard.
expected: Edit Profile should expose the reducer/barlow factor and preserve it, and the computed f/ratio and image scale should match what the profile actually stores (f/4.4, 1.76 arcsec/px). A no-op open+save must never mutate the profile.
repro: 1. Complete onboarding with telescope library 'Sky-Watcher Esprit 100ED' (550mm/100mm), reducer 0.80, pixel size 3.76um. Review screen shows 'Focal length 550.0 mm x 0.80', 'Image scale 1.76 arcsec/px'. 2. sqlite3 <db> 'select focal_length,focal_ratio from equipment_profiles' -> 440.0 | 4.4. 3. Equipment > Edit Profile > scroll to Optical Train: shows f/5.5 and Scale 1.41"/px. 4. Click 'Save Changes' without editing anything. 5. Re-query: 550.0 | 5.5.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-optics2.png (wizard: 440.0 mm, f/4.40, 1.76 arcsec/px), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/equipment-shell-30-review.png (summary: 550.0 mm x 0.80, 1.76 arcsec/px), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-ep2.png (Edit Profile: f/5.5, 1.41"/px, no reducer field); DB before/after captured in-session: focal_length 440.0->550.0, focal_ratio 4.4->5.5
proposed_fix: Add a Reducer/Barlow factor field to the Edit Profile Optical Train section, seeded from the profile; compute effective focal length = telescope_focal_length * reducer and store that in focal_length exactly as the wizard does. Until then, at minimum make Edit Profile round-trip focal_length rather than recomputing it from telescope_focal_length. A 25% image-scale error breaks plate-solve scale hints, framing FOV and guider px->arcsec calibration.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live end-to-end. Seeded a wizard-shaped profile (focal_length=440.0, focal_ratio=4.4, telescope_focal_length=550.0, aperture=100.0), opened Equipment > Edit Profile (screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-07-optical.png shows Focal Length 550.0, f/5.5, Scale 1.41"/px against a profile that stores 440.0/f4.4/1.76"/px), clicked Save Changes with zero edits, and re-queried: 550.0 | 100.0 | 5.5 | 550.0. Mechanism confirmed in code: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/onboarding_provider.dart:408-413 writes focalLength = focalLengthMm * reducerFactor but telescopeFocalLength = the RAW focalLengthMm; packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/dialogs/profile_editor_dialog.dart:209-212 seeds the Focal Length field from telescopeFocalLength in preference to focalLength; profile_editor_dialog/profile_data_operations.dart:517,546-548 then writes that same value back into BOTH focalLength and focalRatio. A grep for reducer/barlow across packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/ returns zero hits, so the reducer really is wizard-only. Severity corrected P0->P1: it is silent and corrupts plate-solve scale hints / FOV / guider px->arcsec, but it is not unrecoverable as claimed -- typing 440 into Focal Length round-trips correctly (both columns then hold 440); only the reducer as a separate concept is unrepresentable.

title: INDI 'Test Connection' reports a green 'Connected' against a host that does not exist
what_happened: Settings > Equipment > Connection > INDI Server Address > Configure > Test Connection returned a green tick and 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' with nothing listening on localhost:7624 (verified: ss shows no listener, /dev/tcp connect returns 'Connection refused', no indiserver process). I then changed the host to 192.0.2.77 (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1, guaranteed unroutable) and pressed Test again: after a real ~30s attempt it again reported the green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' The same app's PHD2 test on the very same screen correctly reports 'No response on localhost:4400. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?', so this is not a platform limitation.
expected: 'Test Connection' must report failure when the TCP connect fails, e.g. 'No response on 192.0.2.77:7624'. Reporting success is worse than no test at all: a user with a Raspberry Pi INDI server who typos the address gets a green tick and then spends the night hunting the wrong problem.
repro: 1. Ensure no indiserver is running. 2. Settings > Equipment > Connection > 'INDI Server Address' > Configure. 3. Click 'Test Connection' with localhost:7624 -> green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' 4. Replace host with 192.0.2.77, click Test Connection -> same green success.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-indi2.png (localhost:7624 green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-indi4.png (192.0.2.77 same green result); port verification: `ss -ltnp | grep 7624` empty, `/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/7624` -> Connection refused, `pgrep indiserver` empty
proposed_fix: Treat a failed TCP connect / handshake timeout as failure and surface the socket error, mirroring the PHD2 test's wording. Distinguish 'connected, 0 devices' (server up, no drivers loaded) from 'could not reach host'.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Verified nothing was listening (ss -ltn | grep 7624 empty, pgrep indiserver empty, /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/7624 -> Connection refused), then Settings > Equipment > Connection > INDI Server Address > Configure > Test Connection returned the green tick 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/eqv-26-inditest.png). The reporter did not name the actual cause; I did: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-102 (_discoverAddressDevices) wraps the bridge call in try/catch, logs a warning and returns const <DeviceInfo>[]. The Rust side is correct -- api_discover_indi_at_address (native/.../bridge/src/api/discovery.rs:153-168) maps the failure to SkotiqError::connection_failed and IndiClient::connect (native/.../indi/src/client.rs:780-794) returns ConnectionFailed on a refused socket -- so the dialog's own catch branch (indi_server_dialog.dart:129-137, 'Connection failed: $e') is simply unreachable. Severity P1 confirmed.
